content:
I'm struggling to show termination of a rather simple while-loop, which I think would be easy to verify with ghost variables. However, as far as I can tell, there currently isn't any notion of ghost variables in Lean/mvcgen (except those variables which are introduced only as part of spec theorems). I'm wondering if I'm simply missing the right approach, or if this is genuinely difficult to prove without ghost variables.

The while-loop I'm interested in iterates over a queue. At each iteration, the head of the queue is removed and (possibly) more items are added to the queue. Termination follows from the fact (assumption below) that we never add the same element to the queue multiple times, and the domain of elements is finite. So e.g., if 2 ever appeared in the queue, we will never add it again. Thus, the queue must at some point run out.

Code for this is given below, with alg being the while-loop, Item being the finite domain and update being the function which removes the head of the queue and then potentially adds more (new) items to the queue.

import Std
open Std Do

#version -- Lean 4.32.0

abbrev Item := Fin 100

structure State where
  queue : List Item
  deriving Nonempty

def update (tl : List Item) : StateM State Unit := do
  -- Shrinks the queue.
  modify ({ · with queue := tl })
  -- Assumption: No element of `Item` is ever added to the queue more than once.
  sorry

def alg : StateM State Unit := do
  while let { queue := _ :: tl } ← get do
    update tl

To prove termination of alg with mvcgen, I want to show:

theorem alg_terminates : ⦃⌜True⌝⦄ alg ⦃⇓_ => ⌜True⌝⦄ := by
  mvcgen [alg]
  case inv1 => sorry -- termination measure
  all_goals sorry

My problem is how to state a termination measure which captures the notion of "all items which have appeared in the queue at some point". With ghost variables, I would add a field seen : HashSet Item to the State, add any new items to seen as part of the update function, and then state the termination measure as something like List.finRange 100 |>.removeAll seen |>.length (this probably isn't exactly right).

Is it possible to somehow work around this by cleverly introducing ghost variables only as part of alg_terminates?
